newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's DRAM prices rebound -- newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Japan's DRAM prices rebound -- newspaper.

text.p: Japanese chip makers and large-lot chip users, including personal computer makers, have agreed to a 5-10 percent price increase for 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips, a Japanese business daily reported at the weekend.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the price increase was mainly due to improved supply and demand conditions as chip makers have refrained from increasing production.
The benchmark "X4" chips will likely be sold to personal computer makers at around 820-930 yen, the paper said.
The price rise for the 16-megabit chips will also help increase demand for the next-generation 64 megabit chips as it narrows the price difference between the two chips, the paper said.
Prices of 16-megabit chips plunged 80 percent in 1996 as production costs fell and competition increased among chip makers, the paper said.
The price falls came even though demand for 16-megabit chips increased by about 60-70 percent last year, it said.
